A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SupGCL, with matching authors, core equations, datasets, and original benchmark results. The main text, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original downstream experiments on TCGA/LINCS-derived GRNs in Tables 2–3, with additional metrics, embedding analyses, and dimension experiments in Appendix F.

after.justification: v4 retains those original experiments and adds temperature ablations, comparator evaluations, link prediction, cross-cancer experiments, robustness tests, and biological enrichment analyses.

M1.justification: The shared encoder, masking operations, joint loss, and Algorithm 1 are retained. However, Equation 6's description changes from a Frobenius inner product to cosine similarity via that product, while the pseudocode still shows inner products. The PDFs do not resolve whether the procedure's normalization changed or the wording corrects an existing implementation.

E1.justification: The original three cancer cohorts and 13 downstream tasks remain. Appendix F.6 adds masked-edge link prediction on breast cancer GRNs, and Appendix G adds mismatched-teacher pretraining, cross-cancer fine-tuning, and direct prediction on unseen cancer types. These substantially expand task and test-scenario coverage without adding new cancer cohorts.

E2.justification: The original five baselines remain in Tables 2–3. v4 additionally evaluates GCA, AFGRL, and SimGRACE against SupGCL on breast cancer hazard and BP tasks in Table 16. Table 17 adds a GCLink-style comparator adapted to the estimated GRNs for link prediction. These are substantive evaluated additions, not merely new citations.

E3.justification: Original benchmark splits, architecture, hyperparameter tables, and fine-tuning protocols are retained. New protocols include link prediction using 500 positive and 500 negative samples with an 80:20 split and masked target edges; temperature and encoder comparisons; patient/teacher subsampling; alternative GRN filtering thresholds; and quantitative clustering and enrichment evaluation. These substantially extend the experimental design.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained PCA and embedding-dimension analyses, v4 tests supervision temperature, Graph Transformer versus GAT within GRACE, cross-cancer transfer, patient and teacher sample sizes, and GRN filtering thresholds. Figure 3 adds quantitative clustering assessment, while Appendix I adds gene-cluster balance and GO/KEGG enrichment analyses. These address supervision, robustness, and biological interpretability questions largely untested in v3.

E5.justification: v3 reports means and standard deviations across folds or seeds without specifying formal significance tests. Appendix F.4 in v4 adds Student's t-tests with Bonferroni correction at 5%, reports four significant comparisons, and states that most comparisons are nonsignificant. The new link-prediction experiment specifies ten seeds, 0–9. Additional repetitions of the original experiments are not established.

E6.justification: The original main and supplementary score tables retain identical means and standard deviations. Substantial new results include temperature, comparator, transfer, robustness, and enrichment findings. For example, Table 17 newly reports SupGCL link-prediction accuracy of 0.763±0.028 and F1 of 0.855±0.018; Figure 3 adds SupGCL NMI/ARI values of 0.117/0.150. These are added evaluations, not improvements over v3 under matched settings.

T1.justification: The stated mathematical definition of simF around Equation 6 changes from a Frobenius inner product to cosine similarity via that product. Theorem 1, its independence assumption, Corollary 1, and the Appendix A derivation remain unchanged. The new explanation motivating independence does not introduce another formal result.

C1.justification: The central method, probabilistic generalization, and superiority claims for the original 13 tasks remain. However, the conclusion changes from saying effectiveness was validated only with matched-cancer teachers to asserting that pretraining on one cancer fails to improve downstream performance on other cancers. This substantively revises the claimed applicability, although Table 18 presents a more mixed picture.

C2.justification: v4 replaces an untested cross-cancer limitation with interpretations of teacher mismatch, fine-tuning transfer, and direct out-of-domain prediction. It also adds explanations concerning supervision strength, limited-data robustness, GRN uncertainty, and pathway-specific biological meaning. Some summaries overgeneralize: Table 4 contains settings below GRACE, and Table 18 preserves lung-to-breast fine-tuning performance despite the conclusion's broad transfer-failure statement.

D1.justification: v4 documents the link-prediction decoder, sigmoid scoring, and BCE loss, plus patient averaging, g:Profiler use, and small-cluster exclusion for enrichment. It corrects GOOtools to GOATOOLS and removes the placeholder code-availability sentence. Existing preprocessing, hyperparameter, hardware, and timing details are largely retained; neither PDF establishes a usable code release.

R1.justification: Related work is substantially reframed around augmentation-free GCL and representation learning from known GRNs. v4 adds discussion and citations for AFGRL, SimGRACE, CancerGATE, and additional GRN literature, while sharpening distinctions from already-cited MuSe-GNN and GCLink. SupGCL is positioned as exploiting measured within-modality perturbations, with explicit separation from multimodal learning and GRN inference.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction's motivation, and related-work narrative are substantially rewritten. Related work gains two focused subsections, the main results narrative is reorganized, and node-level discussion is consolidated in the appendix. An appendix contents page, revised subsection hierarchy, and separate appendix references substantially change navigation and document organization beyond copyediting.

P2.justification: Figure 3 becomes graph-only and gains NMI/ARI annotations; node-level panels are consolidated and redrawn in Figure 4. Figures 7–8 and numerous tables add clustering, enrichment, ablation, transfer, and robustness displays. Existing plots, captions, legends, float placement, title formatting, and page headers are also revised, producing substantial visual changes.

improvement.justification: v4 substantially strengthens the evidence for biological usefulness and applicability, which v3 supported mainly through downstream scores and embedding plots. Relevant comparator tests, biological enrichment, Bonferroni-corrected significance tests, and transfer/robustness experiments make important benefits and boundaries assessable. The gains are tempered by overstatements: Table 4 contradicts the claimed advantage over GRACE in all settings, and Table 18 is more mixed than the conclusion suggests. Nevertheless, the added biological evidence and explicit exposure of statistical and transfer limitations provide a substantial net improvement.
